fluff.overview:
The Inferno is a seventy-five-ton Inner Sphere OmniMech rushed into production by StarCorps Industries on Crofton following the fall of New Avalon to the Draconis Combine Mustered Soldiery during the Dark Age. Introduced in 3146, the design grew out of several improved survivability projects that StarCorps had been developing as testbed concepts, though only one of those made it into the final production model. With generous pod space and heavy armor protection, the Inferno was designed as a flexible heavy platform for the depleted Armed Forces of the Federated Suns.

StarCorps marketed the design with characteristic boldness, promising that the Draconis Combine would not take another inch of Davion soil as long as the Inferno still raged. The chassis quickly became popular within the AFFS, valued both for its combat flexibility and its forgiving handling characteristics that made it accessible to inexperienced MechWarriors.
fluff.capabilities:
The Inferno is built around a standard GM 300 fusion engine and a compact gyro, a combination that frees considerable space in the center torso for heavy weapons. StarCorps engineers took advantage of the StarFrame Heavy Endo Steel chassis to maximize pod capacity while maintaining robust armor protection. In every configuration, the primary weapons are mounted in the center torso (the most heavily armored section of the ’Mech) with additional firepower carried in the side torsos, often in over-the-shoulder mounts. The arms are deliberately left free of weapons, instead equipped with armored gauntlets that allow the Inferno to engage effectively in close combat.

The Prime configuration exemplifies this philosophy, mounting a Heavy PPC as its primary weapon alongside two Medium Re-Engineered Lasers and a pair of MML-5 launchers that provide tactical flexibility between direct and indirect fire support. The design is not particularly fast nor does it carry overwhelming firepower, but its combination of generous pod space, solid protection, and easy handling make it effective for both veteran and inexperienced MechWarriors.

The center torso pod space does suffer from an innovative but insufficiently shielded power link to the fusion engine, producing brief electromagnetic interference that can impair some electronic systems. This was deemed an acceptable trade-off given the urgent need to rebuild AFFS regiments.
fluff.history:
The Inferno’s development was driven by desperation. When New Avalon fell to the Draconis Combine, the Armed Forces of the Federated Suns lost not only their capital but significant manufacturing capacity and strategic depth. StarCorps Industries on Crofton, already engaged in survivability research and testbed projects, was pressed to accelerate development into full production. The result was a design that prioritized practical combat effectiveness over technical perfection.

The AFFS prioritized Inferno shipments to front-line garrisons defending against further Combine incursions, particularly newly formed or rebuilt regiments that needed reliable heavy ’Mechs quickly. The design proved particularly effective as a platform for integrating new MechWarriors, with its easy handling characteristics and forgiving piloting requirements. StarCorps addressed concerns that the Inferno was merely a training platform by providing a shipment of ClanTech-configured Infernos to the Davion Guards, demonstrating the chassis’s ability to carry advanced weapons effectively.

The Kestrel Grenadiers received a lance of Infernos for Operation Perceval. Though not ideally suited to the raiding operations that defined that campaign, the ’Mechs were assigned to base security on Remagen, where they proved effective at harassing enemy landing zones and forcing attackers to disperse their efforts. When Task Force Tsujigiri arrived to end the Federated Suns’ raids, the Infernos engaged each landing in succession, disrupting coordination and keeping the enemy guessing. The Combine pursuit eventually overwhelmed the Grenadiers, trapping them between pursuers and an offloading company.

Infernos have also seen service with the Capellan March Militia, deployed alongside fire support vehicles and battle armor in combined-arms formations. During operations on Taygeta in 3146, Inferno-equipped command lances demonstrated the design’s effectiveness in defensive operations, holding fortified positions against Capellan assaults while protecting attached artillery batteries.
fluff.deployment: Alternate Configuration R distinguishes itself through the use of Clan-specification weapons, reflecting StarCorps’ access to advanced technology during the ilClan era. The center torso mounts an ER PPC and a pair of ER Large Lasers tied into a Clan-grade targeting computer, delivering devastating accuracy at extended range. Two Clan SRM-6 launchers in the side torsos provide close-range punch, sharing a single ton of ammunition in a CASE II-protected bay. Seven additional double heat sinks are required to manage the massive heat load generated by the energy-heavy loadout, making this the most firepower-intensive configuration available.
